verdict.reasoning: Patient reports, “struggling with fever for the past week… about seven days,” and describes “really hot and sweaty,” “aching all over,” feeling “quite nauseous,” and “just generally quite tired and unwell,” which matches 7 days of fever with sweats, myalgias, nausea, and fatigue.

Patient describes “periods of when you're feeling hot, and also periods when you're feeling cold,” and says OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol are “not really helping… Perhaps slightly… it does take the edge off a bit,” consistent with intermittent hot/cold sweats and mild response to antipyretics.
Patient states, “I’ve not been able to eat very much, and I have been drinking but it’s been quite a small amount,” which supports decreased oral intake but some fluids.

Doctor states, “there’s no apparent reason from what you’ve told me… if we can’t find a focus of infection, then that’s… an outstanding question,” indicating no clear infectious focus identified from history.

Patient denies multiple symptoms: no cough/cold/sore throat (“Mmm, not those sort of symptoms”), no ear pain (“my ears are fine”), no diarrhoea (“not really no”), no neck stiffness (“my neck's been fine”), no urinary symptoms or painful urination or frequency, no rash (“I haven’t noticed any rashes”), and no swollen/tender joints (“not really… often have problems with back pain but not really any other joints”).

Patient notes headaches are “just like the general headaches… from staring at the screen,” and has “struggled with [them] through years… related to… screen use, or… changes in weather patterns,” supporting chronic nonspecific headaches related to screen use and weather.
